channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Datafolha: apoio de Bolsonaro influencia mais que o de Lula em SP
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows that Jair Bolsonaro's endorsement has more influence on voter choice for the São Paulo gubernatorial race than Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's. While 27% of voters say they would 'definitely' vote for a candidate backed by Bolsonaro, only 19% say the same for Lula-backed candidates. This indicates Bolsonaro's continued political sway in São Paulo despite not holding office.

item.title: Lula lamenta morte de Waldemar Borges
item.description: President Lula mourned the death of state deputy Waldemar Borges, husband of Minister Luciana Santos, highlighting his nearly 40-year political trajectory in Pernambuco, including roles in the governments of Miguel Arraes and Eduardo Campos, and his service as city councilor and state legislator. Borges died of cancer at age 77, leaving a legacy of social commitment and democratic advocacy.

item.title: Ferramenta do TSE mostra participação do eleitorado no exterior
item.description: The TSE launched the Electoral Data Panel for Voters Abroad, an interactive tool that consolidates historical information on the profile, geographic distribution, and participation of Brazilians eligible to vote overseas. Voter registration data for 2026 will be released by the end of July, aiming to support the logistical planning of the Electoral Justice and improve public access to data previously requiring complex spreadsheet extraction. The platform reveals shifts in the migrant voter profile, including rejuvenation in new poles like Canada and aging in traditional destinations like Japan.

item.title: Flávio assiste jogo Brasil x Noruega de Washington
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ), a pre-candidate for president, will watch the Brazil vs. Norway match from Washington, D.C., without attending the stadium in New York. He arrived in the U.S. on Sunday morning (July 5) and will participate, on Tuesday (July 7), in a public hearing regarding the U.S. tariff increase on Brazilian exports, arguing against raising tariffs up to 25%. After his stay, which ends Wednesday (July 8), Flávio is expected to travel to Ceará to support the Senate pre-candidacy launch of state deputy Alcides Fernandes (PL), within a broader PL strategy backing Ciro Gomes (PSDB) for governor.

item.title: Governo de SP investe R$ 64 bi em universidades de 2023 a 2026
item.description: The São Paulo state government announced R$ 64 billion in investments for state universities (USP, Unicamp, and Unesp) from 2023 to 2026, representing a 28.9% increase compared to the previous period. The funding includes R$ 5 billion from Fapesp for scientific research and R$ 32.5 million to expand the São Paulo Innovation Environments System, which grew from 41 to 101 accredited environments. Governor Tarcísio de Freitas emphasized innovation as a driver of development, aiming to transform knowledge into technological solutions and generate jobs.

item.title: A ponte de Lula não leva a lugar nenhum
item.description: Lula was criticized for inaugurating a non-existent bridge and an empty water pipe, actions seen as electoral maneuvers just before the period that bans government campaigning. The O Antagonista article claims the president is seeking re-election at any cost, even if it involves deceptive public spending. The bridge is portrayed as a symbol of empty promises and political use of infrastructure.

item.title: Por que Tarcísio tem pouco incentivo para entrar de cabeça na campanha de Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: Tarcísio de Freitas has little incentive to actively support Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign, as his own re-election in São Paulo is already strong and he wishes to avoid association with controversies involving the senator, such as those tied to Daniel Vorcaro and U.S. trade tensions. With no political or personal obligation to assist Flávio, Tarcísio may choose to focus on his governance after a potential first-round victory. His support is not guaranteed, despite being strategic for Flávio's chances against Lula.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro chega aos Estados Unidos para audiência sobre tarifas de Trump
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) arrived in the United States to attend a USTR public hearing on the 25% tariffs imposed by the Trump administration on Brazilian exports, claiming the measure is politically motivated and calling for its immediate suspension. He argues the tariff rewards wrongdoers and has been turned into an accusation of treason against the opposition. President Lula responded by saying the Bolsonaro family seeks to submit to American interests through submission.

item.title: Oito makes fáceis e lindíssimas para se inspirar e vibrar pelo Brasil
item.description: Brazil faces Norway in the Round of 16 of the 2026 World Cup, aiming for a historic sixth title and sparking national excitement. The Vida & Estilo section of Metrópoles offers makeup ideas inspired by the national team’s colors — blue, yellow, and green — for fans to show support during matches. Suggestions range from subtle to bold, featuring eyeliners, eyeshadows, and lip products that blend patriotism with personal style.

item.title: Flávio faz “desafio da Copa” em mercado: churrasco com R$ 100
item.description: Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) posted a video challenging inflation by attempting to buy a barbecue with R$100 at a market, giving up items like picanha and linguiça to stay within budget. He criticized President Lula, claiming it was 'the last time you deceived the Brazilian people,' and invited others to post similar videos to compare living costs.

item.title: Audiência digital despenca com Copa do Mundo, e campanha de Flávio passa a usar futebol de trampolim
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro’s (PL-RJ) campaign is adjusting its digital strategy after a drop in social media engagement due to the World Cup. To counter the distraction, the team is using football as a hook to sustain political messaging, particularly criticisms of the Lula government and public security. The first video in the series, posted on YouTube, shows Flávio displaying his football jersey collection, aiming to project a lighter, more approachable image for centrist voters, while Instagram will be used to promote the video.

item.title: Cadastro de missão de observação eleitoral acaba neste domingo
item.description: The deadline for registering National Electoral Observation Missions (MOE Nacional) ends this Sunday, July 5, 2026. Interested entities must apply through the TSE’s electronic system to support transparency, integrity, and public trust in the October elections. Observers must meet strict impartiality, diversity, and non-partisanship requirements, with no ties to political parties or public office.

item.title: Datafolha: Em SP, mais eleitores escolheriam candidato ao governo apoiado por Bolsonaro que por Lula
item.description: In São Paulo, support from Jair Bolsonaro for a gubernatorial candidate influences more voters (27%) than support from Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (19%), according to a Datafolha poll. Lula’s endorsement also generates more rejection (54%) compared to 49% for Bolsonaro. Governor Tarcísio de Freitas is positively rated by 45% of São Paulo residents and leads in voting intentions for the Palácio dos Bandeirantes.

item.title: Procurador que denunciou fraude entra em livro de heróis da pátria
item.description: Prosecutor Pedro Jorge de Melo e Silva, assassinated in 1982 for exposing the Manioc Fraud scandal, will have his name inscribed in the Book of Heroes and Heroines of the Fatherland under Law 15.446/2026 signed by President Lula. The initiative, stemming from Bill 3.663/2023 by Senator Teresa Leitão, honors his bravery in uncovering a scheme involving fraudulent Banco do Brasil loans and false agricultural insurance claims in Pernambuco.

item.title: Tarcísio tem 45% de avaliação positiva no governo de São Paulo, diz Datafolha
item.description: Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) has a 45% approval rating among São Paulo voters, with 20% disapproving and 32% rating his administration as regular, according to a Datafolha survey from July 2026. Approval remains stable compared to the March survey, fluctuating within the two-percentage-point margin of error. Public security and health are cited as the state's top concerns, each mentioned by 27% of respondents.

item.title: Caso Michelle move rota de campanha, põe esposa de Flávio no aquecimento e reduz forças no PL Mulher
item.description: Fernanda Bolsonaro, wife of Flávio Bolsonaro, will take a central role in the presidential campaign following the controversial video of Michelle Bolsonaro, undergoing media training and potentially gaining her own social media team to focus on health and women-oriented discourse, with support from economist Daniella Marques. Flávio Bolsonaro publicly repudiated Paulo Figueiredo's comments that women vote poorly, aiming to present himself as more palatable to female voters at an event with female leaders in Brasília.

item.title: Pesquisas eleitorais: como está a disputa Lula x Flávio após números da última semana
item.description: Recent polls show Lula leading Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 presidential race, though with variations between institutes: AtlasIntel/Bloomberg gives Lula a 6.5-point lead in the runoff (48.8% to 42.3%), while BTG/Nexus shows a technical tie (47% to 44%). No third-party candidate breaks the polarization, with Renan Santos and Ronaldo Caiado trailing significantly, and Michelle Bolsonaro failing to emerge as a viable PL alternative in simulation scenarios.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro mordeu a isca e caiu na provocação da madrasta
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro reacted to a provocation by his stepmother, Michelle Bolsonaro, after she shared a video implying his presence at a nude party involving ex-banker Daniel Vorcaro. He denied any connection with Vorcaro beyond discussions about his father's film and accused Michelle of being misinformed or manipulated, despite acknowledging her work in PL Mulher. The right-wing women's meeting in Brasília ended in failure due to a boycott by key right-wing legislators.

item.title: TSE libera propaganda intrapartidária
item.description: The Superior Electoral Court (TSE) has authorized pre-candidates for the 2026 elections to begin intraparty propaganda activities starting this Sunday, May 5, directed exclusively at party members and delegates. This phase does not constitute an open campaign to the electorate and aims to influence internal party selections. The measure follows the official electoral calendar for the 2026 vote.

item.title: Governo de SP responde PSOL-Rede e diz que canais oficiais divulgam ações de interesse público
item.description: The São Paulo government responded to the PSOL-Rede representation, stating that official channels only disclose actions of public interest, in reply to criticisms regarding posts involving the state’s basic sanitation company (Sabesp). The defense emphasized that there is no improper use of public resources for personal promotion.

item.title: Datafolha: Tarcísio é aprovado por 63% e desaprovado por 32% em SP
item.description: A July 2026 Datafolha poll shows that São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas has 63% approval and 32% disapproval, with 45% of voters rating his administration as 'excellent' or 'good'. The survey interviewed 1,608 voters from July 1–3, with a 2-point margin of error and 95% confidence level.

item.title: Com Haddad rejeitado por 47%, Tarcísio abre 16 pontos no segundo turno, diz Datafolha
item.description: A Datafolha poll shows Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leading Fernando Haddad (PT) 53% to 37% in a hypothetical runoff for São Paulo governor. Haddad faces 47% rejection among voters, while Tarcísio has 29%. Both candidates showed stability since March, with Tarcísio edging up from 52% to 53% and Haddad unchanged at 37%.

item.title: Tarcísio tem 45% de avaliação positiva em SP, diz Datafolha
item.description: The Datafolha poll released on Sunday (5) shows that 45% of São Paulo residents rate Governor Tarcísio de Freitas' administration as excellent or good, 32% as fair, and 20% as poor or terrible. The results indicate stability compared to the previous survey, keeping the governor with a positive but sub-majority approval rating.

item.title: O que fez Centrão colocar o pé no freio sobre possível apoio a Flávio Bolsonaro
item.description: The Centrão, initially inclined to support Flávio Bolsonaro’s presidential pre-candidacy, delayed its decision due to controversy over his relationship with Daniel Vorcaro of Banco Master and public statements by Michelle Bolsonaro, who accused him of disrespect. The uncertainty generated by these factors has caused centrist parties to hold back their endorsement, awaiting further developments before committing.

item.title: Código de ética, Bolsonaro e eleições pautam STF no 2º semestre
item.description: The STF resumes hearings in August with a politically charged docket, including supplementary elections in RJ and RR, revisions to the Clean Record Law, a proposed Code of Ethics for justices, and investigations involving Bolsonaro and the January 8 events. Chief Justice Edson Fachin will oversee the judiciary’s recess duty until July 19, after which Alexandre de Moraes will act as interim president. Justice Cármen Lúcia rapporteurs the Ethics Code despite internal dissent, with hopes of presenting it in plenary session by year-end.

item.title: Quantas propostas para reduzir a maioridade penal há no Congresso? Entenda
item.description: In the National Congress, there are 32 PECs and 307 legislative proposals in the Chamber of Deputies, plus 7 PECs in the Senate, addressing the reduction of the age of criminal responsibility. PEC 32/2015, approved by the CCJ in June, lowers the age to 16 generally, while other proposals, such as those by Captain Alden and Júlia Zanatta (PL), advocate for the change only in cases of serious crimes. The issue is gaining electoral traction due to strong public support — 79% according to DataFolha — even among Lula voters, driven by high-profile crimes involving adolescents.

item.title: Pesquisa Datafolha mostra Tarcísio de Freitas com 45% de aprovação em São Paulo
item.description: Datafolha poll shows São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas maintains 45% approval for his administration, unchanged since March, with 32% rating it as fair and 20% as poor or terrible. Personal approval stands at 63%, with 32% disapproving and 6% undecided. The survey interviewed 1,608 voters aged 16+ across 71 municipalities from April 1–3, with a 2-point margin of error at 95% confidence.

item.title: Vereadora pivô de crise entre Flávio e Michelle prega união e diz não querer ‘alimentar conflito’
item.description: Fortaleza councilwoman Priscila Costa (PL-CE) says she does not seek to fuel conflict between Michelle and Flávio Bolsonaro, urging unity among the right to defeat the PT in the 2026 elections. She was overlooked for the Senate nomination in Ceará, a decision that intensified the family rift after the PL chose Alcides Fernandes as its candidate with Flávio’s backing. Priscila reaffirmed her support for the PL’s presidential pre-candidate and called for the right to remain united despite internal divisions.

item.title: Nova lei amplia direitos de pessoas com diabetes tipo 1
item.description: Law 15.439/26 expands rights for people with type 1 diabetes, ensuring access to medication and supplies via SUS, breaks for glucose monitoring and insulin administration in schools and workplaces, reasonable accommodations, anti-discrimination protections, and inclusion of health data in the National Identity Card. President Lula sanctioned the law, vetoing a provision that conditioned financial benefits on a specific biopsychosocial assessment, arguing it would create unnecessary barriers. The law also allows for recognition as a person with disability under the Statute of Persons with Disabilities, subject to meeting established criteria, without automatic classification.

item.title: TSE: pré-candidatos já podem fazer propaganda intrapartidária
item.description: The TSE authorized intraparty propaganda for pre-candidates starting July 5, allowing them to promote their candidacies among party members and delegates during conventions (July 20 to August 5) and up to 15 days before primaries, with bans on radio, TV, and outdoor advertising. Such propaganda must be removed after conventions and does not constitute premature electoral campaigning if it does not explicitly request votes. Violations may incur fines from R$ 5,000 to R$ 25,000 or the equivalent cost of the propaganda.

item.title: O cenário da disputa pelo governo de São Paulo, segundo novo Datafolha
item.description: The latest Datafolha poll shows Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leading the São Paulo gubernatorial race with 46% voter intent, while Fernando Haddad (PT) trails at 30%. Other candidates remain marginal, with Vera Lúcia (PSTU) at 5% and others below that threshold. In a potential runoff, Tarcísio holds 53% to Haddad’s 37%.

item.title: Por que esquecemos em quem votamos?
item.description: Brazilians' inability to recall the names of their senators or federal deputies does not reflect civic apathy, but rather the incentives created by Brazil's open-list proportional representation system in nationwide districts. This system fosters indirect representation through local intermediaries — such as mayors, community leaders, and organizations — who mobilize votes and monitor parliamentary performance, making individual name recognition less necessary for electoral success. Parliamentary amendments, which allow deputies to direct resources to localities, reinforce these intermediary networks, meaning that low name recall is a feature of the system's design, not necessarily a sign of democratic failure.

item.title: Em 1º turno, Tarcísio tem 46%, Haddad 30% e demais candidatos, 13%
item.description: Governor of São Paulo Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicans) leads the Datafolha poll with 46% voting intentions in the first round of the 2026 elections, followed by Fernando Haddad (PT) with 30%. Other candidates combined account for 13% of voting intentions.

item.title: O vice 'campeão de votos' de Renan Santos
item.description: Renan Santos (Missão) announced Lieutenant Colonel Aroldo Medina as his vice-presidential running mate for the 2026 elections. Medina performed modestly in the 2024 municipal elections in Porto Alegre, placing 265th with 222 votes. The selection appears to be a strategic move to garner additional support, despite his previous low vote count.

item.title: Flávio só marca gol contra (por Mary Zaidan)
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro is repeatedly making political mistakes, from lying about the Pix system to actions that harm his own campaign, such as urging the delay of U.S. tariffs to help Lula. His allies and even his stepmother Michelle have criticized his actions as disastrous and self-sabotaging. Despite positioning himself as a Trump ally and defending Pix, he distorts historical facts and ignores his own contradictions, including his requests for money from Daniel Vorcaro.

item.title: De olho em interesses particulares, Lula, STF e Congresso aceleram farra das despesas
item.description: The Supreme Federal Court (STF) relaxed its own austerity rules, authorizing payment of 'penduricalhos' to judges that can push their earnings above the constitutional ceiling, yielding to corporate pressure. Despite consensus that the 2026 election winner will need fiscal adjustment to avoid running out of funds, the three branches continue approving spending increases to serve particular interests and lobbies. The STF decision seeks to legalize practices already occurring via administrative rulings, amid the Court's image crisis and some justices' implication in the Banco Master scandal.

item.title: TSE libera propaganda interna de pré-candidatos neste domingo
item.description: The TSE authorizes, starting this Sunday (Jul 5, 2026), internal party propaganda by pre-candidates to persuade party members and delegates to support their candidacies ahead of conventions from July 20 to August 5. Public electoral campaigning remains prohibited until August 16, with the first round of elections on October 4 and the second on October 25. Direct or indirect vote-seeking remains banned even in public appearances or interviews until then.

item.title: Renan Santos lidera vaquinha eleitoral com mais de R$ 1 milhão
item.description: Renan Santos, a presidential pre-candidate from the Missão party, leads virtual fundraising for the 2026 Brazilian elections with over R$1.1 million raised in 50 days after the TSE authorized donations. The QueroApoiar platform reports that ten pre-candidates have collectively raised nearly R$3 million through online donations, highlighting the growing role of crowdfunding in Brazilian political campaigns.

item.title: Leonardo Barreto na Crusoé: Rebelião no bolsonarismo
item.description: Deputy Marco Feliciano (PL-SP) publicly criticized Flávio Bolsonaro on social media, dismissing claims of an evangelical conspiracy against his candidacy. He argued that evangelicals are not plotting against him, using direct and symbolic language to reject the narrative. The post was first published on O Antagonista, highlighting internal divisions within the bolsonarist movement.

item.title: PT quer emplacar ex-chefe de gabinete de Haddad como suplente de Tebet
item.description: PT leaders are seeking to place Laio Morais, former chief of staff to Fernando Haddad, as Simone Tebet’s (PSB) Senate running mate in São Paulo for 2026. The move hinges on Lula’s re-election and a potential invitation for Tebet to join his government, which would vacate her Senate seat for the PT ally. Tebet’s allies deny any prior agreement, insisting the choice of alternates rests solely with her and the PSB.

item.title: Alta de Raquel Lyra faz aliados apostarem em neutralidade de Lula com João Campos
item.description: The sudden rise of Raquel Lyra in recent polls has led her allies to believe that Lula may choose neutrality in João Campos’ campaign, to avoid alienating Raquel’s voters in a highly competitive presidential race.

item.title: Tarcísio abre 16 pontos de vantagem sobre Haddad em SP, diz Datafolha
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas (Republicanos) leads the race for the Palácio dos Bandeirantes with 46% of voting intentions, according to a Datafolha poll. Former Finance Minister Fernando Haddad (PT) follows in second place with 30%, a 16-point gap. Tarcísio would also defeat Haddad in a potential runoff.

item.title: Aliados de Flávio suspeitam de influência de ministro em ataque de Michelle
item.description: Allies of Flávio Bolsonaro suspect that Michelle Bolsonaro’s attack on her stepson was influenced by information allegedly supplied by Minister André Mendonça, rapporteur of the Master case at the STF, who has authority to authorize PF operations. Though possibly conspiratorial, the theory is treated as plausible within Flávio’s inner circle. The article is subscriber-only and requires registration for full access.

item.title: Novo plano de energia estabelece R$ 2,8 tri para fósseis
item.description: The 2035 Decennial Energy Expansion Plan (PDE) projects R$ 3.5 trillion in energy investments through 2035, with R$ 2.8 trillion (80%) allocated to fossil fuels — primarily oil and natural gas — while renewables receive only R$ 374 billion. The plan allocates R$ 596 billion to the electric matrix, emphasizing biofuels (R$ 115B), wind (R$ 79B), and transmission (R$ 117B), but warns that distributed generation (MMGD) expansion could overload the grid and trigger curtailment.

item.title: Em ritmo de campanha, Lula teve agendas em 13 municípios de sete estados em 30 dias
item.description: In campaign mode, President Lula held agendas in 13 municipalities across seven states over the past 30 days. He urged ministers in a recent meeting to accelerate government deliveries before the electoral blackout, which bans inaugurations of public works starting July 3. The article emphasizes the pressure to meet targets ahead of the campaign restriction period.

item.title: Sidônio fica mal com o PT da Bahia após orientar Lula a se afastar de Jaques Wagner
item.description: Sidônio Palmeira fell out with the Bahia PT after advising President Lula to distance himself from Senator Jaques Wagner to avoid associating the president with Wagner’s involvement in the Master Case. The advice caused discomfort within the state party, which regards Wagner as an important figure. The article is subscriber-only.

item.title: Michael Jordan e a amarelinha: geopolítica, soft power e seleção brasileira
item.description: The partnership between the Brazilian Football Confederation (CBF) and the Jordan brand for Brazil’s 2026 World Cup kit reflects a soft power strategy aligned with Brazil’s foreign policy, aiming to manage U.S. relations amid recent geopolitical tensions, including the U.S.-Israel strike on Iran and volatile Lula-Trump dynamics. Though aesthetically controversial, the jersey symbolizes a symbolic rapprochement with the U.S., avoiding direct confrontation while upholding constitutional principles of non-intervention and peace.

item.title: Flávio estava no Brasil na época da "Noite das Astronautas" em NY
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro was in Brazil between May 12 and 16, 2024, attending in-person Senate sessions on May 14 and 15, according to official records, which rules out his presence at Daniel Vorcaro’s 'Astronauts’ Night' in New York during the same period. The claim of his attendance at the party was raised by Michelle Bolsonaro amid a family feud but lacks concrete evidence.

item.title: Chamada de "fenômeno" por Valdemar, Michelle segue firme e não recua
item.description: Valdemar Costa Neto praised Michelle Bolsonaro as a 'phenomenon' of charisma and leadership on Noblat's program, but analysis suggests this praise is a behind-the-scenes effort to ease internal PL tensions and rescue Flávio Bolsonaro's campaign from isolation, pressuring Michelle to retract her criticisms of her stepson. Michelle, however, refused to perform any public act of contrition, rejecting the idea of sacrificing her political capital to benefit a family that has historically marginalized and disrespected her, thereby undermining any artificial unity the party seeks to impose.

item.title: Pesquisas mostram Flávio como único nome da direita a rivalizar com Lula
item.description: Polls released in June and July 2024 show Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) as the only right-wing figure capable of rivaling President Lula (PT) in a potential 2026 presidential runoff, maintaining technical ties or differences within the margin of error. Despite the public split with Michelle Bolsonaro and internal crises on the right, Flávio retains between 42% and 44% of voter intentions in the runoff scenario, concentrating most of the Bolsonarist electorate. The Nexus and AtlasIntel/Bloomberg polls, despite differing methodologies, confirm his electoral resilience even after Michelle’s accusations of disrespect.
